report.title: Test and Evaluation of Vehicle Platooning Proof-of-Concept Based on Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control
report.authors: Tim A. Tiernan, Nicholas Richardson, Philip Azeredo, Wassim G. Najm, Taylor Lochrane
report.locators: Table 12 pp. 44–45, section 4.3.2 and footnote 7, section 4.3.4 and Appendix C pp. 91–102.

analysis: The federal report describes asynchronous CAN, ADMAS and radio logs being rounded to the nearest 20 Hz grid, ties discarded and slow fields left blank. The 1 Hz brake light can be held. CSV columns have different source instruments and original rates. Compare elapsed ticks within a run, count exact duplicates across all 478 parsed fields and exclude all surviving distinct rows in ambiguous within-run bins. One-row run labels are retained for coverage only.

Compare ADMAS and PRISM Speed Of Service (SOS, seconds in Appendix C) as paired nonmissing fields for each source-column colour prefix and vehicle suffix. Time Of Observation (TOO) is a separate epoch-seconds field on each endpoint. Counts at similar times or on two instrument layers do not produce a packet emission denominator. The report uses the sending observation for BSM binning. PRISM and ADMAS have different observation points.

On identical bins compare speed_CACC(t) with velocity_fwd_PINPOINT(t) or velocity_fwd_PINPOINT(t-16s), both m/s. No interpolation. Specific −16 s comparison motivated by report footnote 7. An independent Socrata extraction of the three selected speed/time columns was used to cross-check the direction in runs 50–53 and 69–72. All-field conflict screening can retain fewer bins than a four-column query.

In the eight five-car comparisons identified in Table 12 and the performance figures, use the black lead car and the ordered follower list as published. Compare PinPoint forward-speed crossings at 52.5 mph (23.4696 m/s). Arm down/up criteria after 5 s above 25 or below 21 m/s. Require 0.4 s past the midpoint and break sequences on gaps >0.15 s. Use first leader downward crossing and first later upward crossing, and a unique same-direction follower candidate within ±15 s. This is a speed-transition timing measurement on the published time grid. Authors used acceleration thresholding in §4.3.4. Neither method isolates radio transport or actuator dynamics.

The source flags a mapping problem for group position and distance and a scaling issue for injected torque. The XLSX gives m/s² for average ADMAS acceleration while Appendix C gives g. No unit conversion or causal motor-latency estimate uses these fields.
coverage_desc: Complete 1,204,993,696-byte 478-column CSV and both documentation attachments read, with independent per-run query; aggregate comparisons use no raw coordinates or vehicle traces in the published package.
reproduction: Download the exact bulk URL from bulk.url as full.csv (optionally gzip locally), and query run_counts.url as run-list.json. Run python derive_fhwa.py full.csv run-list.json OUT using Python 3.11+, NumPy and pandas. Allow scratch space for compressed per-run records.

physical_motion.scope: See per-run, per-position and direction numbers in fhwa-paired-motion.csv.
